chapter.title: CLI apps
chapter.lede: `args()` is the argument list. `std/args` reads flags and options from it, and `std/cli` builds the whole command from a record type.

sections.heading: Reading arguments
prose: std/args takes a token list. cli() takes the real arguments; cliOf(list) takes a list you supply, which is how a test checks the parsing without a process.
flag asks whether a token is present. opt reads --name=value and --name value, and answers Option<String>. positionals returns what is left, and rest returns what follows --.

sections.heading: std/cli
prose: std/cli goes further. Declare a record whose fields are the options, and give each field a validated type with its own documentation line. cli("./module") reflects it into a parser and a help text, so no flag name is written twice.
A parse answers Valid or Invalid with the issues attached to their fields, so a program reports every problem at once instead of the first one.
